newsitem.title: UK: BIB confident of winning regulatory approval.
newsitem.headline: BIB confident of winning regulatory approval.

text.p: Partners in British Interactive Broadcasting (BIB) are confident that their 200-channel digital services venture will win necessary regulatory approval necessary, a British Telecom official said.

"We have spent many months in discussion with a broad range of regulatory authorities. All parties concerned welcome the initiative and the services we will be introducing, said Rupert Gavin, BT's director of multimedia services.

Gavin was addressing a press briefing after the announcement early on Wednesday that BT is to join forces with British pay television giant BSkyB and Midland Bank and Matsushita Electric of Japan as partners in a new consortium to supply services such as home shopping and home banking.

The BIB partners are to provide 265 million pounds ($433 million) to bring the retail price of decoder boxes for the services down to 200 pounds or less. The venture is expected to break even after five years.

BSkyB, in which Rupert Murdoch's News Corp is the largest shareholder, previously said it planned to launch digital satellite services late this year but now aims for a Spring 1998 start. Interactive services should become available later in 1998.
BSkyB and BT will each have stakes of 32.5 percent in the BIB consortium, while Midland Bank will hold 20 percent and Matsushita the remaining 15 percent.
The combination of Britain's leading pay television company with the dominant telephone company is certain to be examined closely by regulators.
BSkyB deputy managing director David Chance told Reuters that the company had spent months talking to Oftel and was confident that the telecoms watchdog would give its blessing.
BT's Gavin said the BIB partners had also talked with the European Commission and both the incoming and outgoing British governments but that "those discussions are not complete".
"But we have a high degree of confidence that the package we introduce will not be significantly different (from that outlined today)," he said.
Oftel said it was to look closely at how the venture intends to operate but that it was not its role to approve the deal. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
